result.title: DeltaHarness: Self-Evolving Harnesses for Resource-Adaptive Tool Execution
result.summary: Tool-using agents rely on execution harnesses to organize and schedule tool operations. The same task and resource description can conceal runtime conditions that reverse the latency ordering of valid execution plans. Resolving this uncertainty requires firsthand execution in the target setting. We introduce DeltaHarness, an execution-guided policy-search method that adapts agent harnesses from cold-start measurements. Its QHI loop uses the observed response to update runtime dispatch, revise physical plans, and select experiments for later proposals. An independent confirmation panel controls policy replacement. With fixed dispatch, a revised materialization policy reduces complete-delivery latency by 30.0% on one video-editing task across three fresh pairs. On held-out tasks, the evolved policies reduce latency by 8.2% relative to the best fixed plan in one seed and by 4.6% relative to the initial proposal in another.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DeltaHarness，一种从冷启动实测数据出发的工具执行 harness 自适应方法，通过 QHI 循环依据观测响应更新运行时调度、修订物化计划并挑选后续实验，并由独立确认面板把关策略替换，以降低任务完成延迟。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用真实执行测量消解计划优劣的不确定性、按成本挑选探测实验并按实测延迟替换策略」的框架，可能与 LVR 中证据获取的收益成本权衡及 LOOK/STOP 决策相近，可供核查；但该文面向工具调度延迟，不涉及视觉推理状态或表示，联系较远。
